name: राजविद्याराजगुह्ययोग
teaching: The secret hidden in plain sight: everything rests in the divine the way wind rests in space — held, pervaded, yet never grasping or grasped. No elaborate rite is needed; a leaf, a flower, water, offered with love, is received. And the door is closed to no one — whoever comes, however late, however fallen, arrives. The sovereign secret is intimacy: the universe rests in Him who is not contained by it, the smallest leaf offered in love is accepted, and no past, however broken, disqualifies refuge. He carries what His lovers lack.
questions: What is the smallest thing you could offer today — and could you actually offer it?
Krishna says he is the same to all beings. Where do you assume you are disqualified?
What would change if you believed nothing devotional is ever lost?

verses.speaker: श्रीभगवानुवाच
verses.devanagari:
इदं तु ते गुह्यतमं प्रवक्ष्याम्यनसूयवे ।
ज्ञानं विज्ञानसहितं यज्ज्ञात्वा मोक्ष्यसेऽशुभात्॥
verses.transliteration:
idaṃ tu te guhyatamaṃ pravakṣyāmyanasūyave
jñānaṃ vijñānasahitaṃ yajjñātvā mokṣyase'śubhāt
verses.essence: To you, who do not cavil, I shall declare this most secret knowledge together with realization — knowing which you will be freed from misfortune.
verses.translation: I shall now declare to thee who does not cavil, the greatest secret, the knowledge combined with experience (Self-realisation). Having known this thou shalt be free evil.

anvaya.base: गुह्य · secret, to be hidden (√गुह् · to hide)

anvaya.meaning: to one who does not cavil
anvaya.base: अनसूयु · free of envy, not fault-finding
anvaya.parts: अन् (not) + असूयु (envious, fault-finding): one who does not find fault
विज्ञान (realization) + सहित (joined with): accompanied by realization
अ (not) + शुभ (auspicious, good): what is not good

verses.explanation: Guhya-tamam — not just secret but the superlative, the innermost chamber. And the entry qualification is named again: anasūyave, to one free of the carping spirit. Secrets of this order are not hidden by locks but by attitude; cynicism cannot hear them even when they are spoken aloud.
verses.connection: Opens the chapter Krishna will call the king of teachings — to the one listener fit to receive it.
verses.reflection: Receive one teaching today the way this chapter is given: as a secret entrusted, not data downloaded.
verses.background: Krishna leans closer, as it were, mid-battlefield: to you who do not cavil, he says, I now declare the most secret knowledge — the royal science, the royal mystery, directly experienceable, righteous, joyful to practice, imperishable. Only the faithless miss it and return to the mortal round.
verses.hook: Who is ready for the deepest teaching, the one that frees from evil?

views.text: "This" points to the knowledge of Brahman already taught, and "tu" marks it off from mere meditation. This knowledge alone is the direct means to liberation; the "evil" escaped is worldly bondage.

The secret knowledge is upāsanā, meditation that has the nature of bhakti. The added vijñāna is knowing how this worship differs from other meditations; it frees from every evil that blocks reaching the Lord.
Freedom from displeasure is named as a key requirement for passing on knowledge, and the pair jñāna and vijñāna is read as knowledge and action.

Vijñāna is worship. The listener qualifies because he does not find fault with a Lord who keeps praising himself out of compassion. Secrets rise in rank: dharma, the Self beyond the body, and highest of all, the supreme Self.
Krishna gives this knowledge to Arjun because he is not envious; those who scorn God's self-praise as conceit cannot benefit, since He praises Himself only to increase the souls' devotion.

verses.devanagari:
राजविद्या राजगुह्यं पवित्रमिदमुत्तमम् ।
प्रत्यक्षावगमं धर्म्यं सुसुखं कर्तुमव्ययम्॥
verses.transliteration:
rājavidyā rājaguhyaṃ pavitramidamuttamam
pratyakṣāvagamaṃ dharmyaṃ susukhaṃ kartumavyayam
verses.essence: This is the king of knowledge, the king of secrets, the supreme purifier — known by direct experience, in accord with dharma, easy to practice, imperishable.
verses.translation: This is the kingly science, the kingly secret, the supreme purifier, realisable by direct intuitional knowledge, according to righteousness, very easy to perform and imperishable.

anvaya.parts: राज (king) + विद्या (science): the king among sciences
राज (king) + गुह्य (secret): the king among secrets

anvaya.base: प्रत्यक्ष · before the eyes; अवगम · understanding
anvaya.parts: प्रत्यक्ष (direct) + अवगम (understanding): whose understanding is direct
सु (very) + सुख (easy, pleasant): very easy
अ (not) + व्यय (decay): that does not decay

verses.explanation: Seven titles, two of them startling: pratyakṣāvagamam — verifiable in one's own experience, not on hearsay — and su-sukham kartum, *easy* and *pleasant* to practice. The supreme secret is not an ordeal but the one discipline that delights as it works. Its only real obstacle, the chapter implies, is disbelief that it could be this direct.
verses.connection: The credentials of the royal teaching — culminating in the chapter's heart, devotion.
verses.reflection: Test the royal claim yourself: this knowing is verifiable here, pleasant to practice, imperishable. Verify.
verses.background: Krishna leans closer, as it were, mid-battlefield: to you who do not cavil, he says, I now declare the most secret knowledge — the royal science, the royal mystery, directly experienceable, righteous, joyful to practice, imperishable. Only the faithless miss it and return to the mortal round.
verses.hook: What makes this knowledge the king of all sciences?

refs.note: Devotion destroys three poisons: past sins, the seeds of sin in the heart, and ignorance, which is why the verse calls this knowledge the supreme purifier.

views.text: Rāja can also come from √rāj, to shine: this knowledge outshines all learning. It burns up the karma of countless births in a moment, is easy like telling jewels apart, and, unlike results of action, never runs out.

"Royal" can mean the science of the broad-minded. Direct perception means the Lord, worshipped with bhakti, becomes immediately perceptible; and the worship is imperishable, since even after giving himself the Lord feels he has done nothing.
Kings like Janaka have the right to this science; it is their guarded secret, and it is easy for warriors because their heroic nature keeps them from wavering.
Pratyakṣāvagama means its fruit is seen here and now, and it is dharmya because it is the fruit of all dharmas.

He reads each epithet as describing devotion: the highest science, hidden so that love stays a free choice, purifying sin, its seeds and ignorance, directly verifiable, and easy because God asks only for love.

verses.devanagari:
अश्रद्दधानाः पुरुषा धर्मस्यास्य परन्तप ।
अप्राप्य मां निवर्तन्ते मृत्युसंसारवर्त्मनि॥
verses.transliteration:
aśraddadhānāḥ puruṣā dharmasyāsya parantapa
aprāpya māṃ nivartante mṛtyusaṃsāravartmani
verses.essence: People without faith in this dharma, Parantapa, fail to reach me and return to the round of death and rebirth.
verses.translation: Those who have no faith in this Dharma (knowledge of the Self), O Parantapa (Arjuna), return to the path of this world of death without attaining Me.

anvaya.parts: अ (not) + श्रद्दधान (trusting): not having faith

anvaya.form: noun, masculine, genitive singular (of; here: faith in)

anvaya.parts: पर (enemy) + तप (one who burns): one who burns his enemies

anvaya.meaning: on the path of deathly rebirth
anvaya.base: मृत्यु · death; संसार · cycle of rebirth; वर्त्मन् · path
anvaya.parts: मृत्यु (death) + संसार (rebirth) + वर्त्मन् (path): the path of rebirth bound up with death

verses.explanation: The single failure mode of an easy path: aśraddhā, the refusal to trust it enough to try. No punishment is decreed — only the default: nivartante, they go on circling, because the exit, though open, was never believed in. Faith here is not credulity but the minimal trust any door requires before it can be walked through.
verses.connection: The one fine-print clause on 9.2's accessibility: ease helps only those who believe in the door.
verses.reflection: Notice the one entrance fee named: faith. Bring some to one practice today and watch the door move.
verses.background: Krishna leans closer, as it were, mid-battlefield: to you who do not cavil, he says, I now declare the most secret knowledge — the royal science, the royal mystery, directly experienceable, righteous, joyful to practice, imperishable. Only the faithless miss it and return to the mortal round.
verses.hook: What happens to those who have no faith in this path?

refs.note: The path begins with faith, then the company of holy people, then personal practice, supporting the verse's point that faithlessness blocks the way at the start.
Life is walked by faith rather than sight, which he uses to show that faith is needed before direct perception of God comes.

views.text: The faithless are those who take the body for the Self and live for pleasure. They miss the Lord so completely that they do not gain even a little devotion, the first step on the path to him.
Even people fit to practise this worship can lack the faith that means eagerness for realization. That such a hindrance arises from past evil karma is called a strange thing.
The genitive is read as an object: they do not accept this dharma of devotion. Even if they strive to reach the Lord by other means, they keep wandering on the road of death.
Faith here is not belief in dogma or in another's word but an unshakable inner conviction that Self-knowledge alone gives peace; it goes hand in hand with fiery determination.
Even the best path is useless to one who will not walk it; faith comes first, as in ordinary life, and those who refuse it keep turning in the cycle of birth and death.

verses.devanagari:
मया ततमिदं सर्वं जगदव्यक्तमूर्तिना ।
मत्स्थानि सर्वभूतानि न चाहं तेष्ववस्थितः॥
verses.transliteration:
mayā tatamidaṃ sarvaṃ jagadavyaktamūrtinā
matsthāni sarvabhūtāni na cāhaṃ teṣvavasthitaḥ
verses.essence: By me, in my unmanifest form, all this universe is pervaded. All beings rest in me; I do not rest in them.
verses.translation: All this world is pervaded by Me in My unmanifest aspect; all beings exist in Me, but I do not dwell in them.

anvaya.form: past passive participle, neuter, nominative singular
adjective, masculine, instrumental singular (by), describing मया
anvaya.parts: अव्यक्त (unmanifest) + मूर्ति (form): one whose form is unmanifest
मत् (in me) + स्थ (standing): standing in me
सर्व (all) + भूत (beings): all beings

verses.explanation: The royal secret begins as paradox: everything rests in him, he rests in nothing — the way all waves are in the ocean while the ocean is not 'in' any wave. Mayā tatam idam sarvam: all this is pervaded by me in unmanifest form; all beings stand in me — na cāhaṃ teṣv avasthitaḥ, and I am not contained in them. Pervasion without containment: he is the ground of each thing without being a tenant of any thing, as space holds everything and is held by nothing. Hold the discomfort; the next verse will deepen it on purpose, revoking even the resting.
verses.connection: First half of the chapter's great paradox — to be deliberately overturned in 9.5.
verses.reflection: Feel once today: everything around you is in Him — and He stands free of all of it.
verses.background: The sovereign paradox is stated: all this world is pervaded by Me; all beings rest in Me — and I am not in them; nor do beings rest in Me. Behold My divine yoga: like wind standing in space, beings stand in Me; nature, under My supervision, produces the moving and unmoving.
verses.hook: How can God pervade everything yet not be contained in anything?

refs.note: One God is hidden in all beings and pervades everything, the same all-pervasion this verse declares.
Everything in the world is pervaded by God, supporting the verse's statement that the whole world is pervaded by Him.
God pervades all that has existed and all that will exist, another Vedic statement of His all-pervasion.

views.text: Beings exist in the Lord because they have reality only through him, their Self. He is not in them because he touches nothing, and what touches nothing cannot sit in anything like contents in a vessel.
He pervades as the unseen inner controller of the Antaryāmi passage; beings rest in him as his body, under his control. "I am not in them" means he does not depend on them for his existence.
When beings show their insentient nature foremost, their inner sentience, the Lord, stays hidden; that hiddenness is what "I am not in them" means.
The world is neither a transformation of God nor an illusion but His material energy, and souls are His higher energy; both lie within Him, yet He exceeds them as the ocean exceeds its waves.

verses.devanagari:
न च मत्स्थानि भूतानि पश्य मे योगमैश्वरम् ।
भूतभृन्न च भूतस्थो ममात्मा भूतभावनः॥
verses.transliteration:
na ca matsthāni bhūtāni paśya me yogamaiśvaram
bhūtabhṛnna ca bhūtastho mamātmā bhūtabhāvanaḥ
verses.essence: And yet beings do not rest in me — behold my divine yoga! Sustaining beings, yet not dwelling in them, my Self is the very source of beings.
verses.translation: Nor do beings exist in Me (in reality); behold My divine Yoga, supporting all beings, but not dwelling in them, is My Self, the efficient cause of beings.

anvaya.parts: मत् (in me) + स्थ (standing): standing in me

anvaya.base: ऐश्वर · belonging to the Lord (from ईश्वर)

anvaya.parts: भूत (beings) + भृत् (bearer): one who bears beings
भूत (beings) + स्थ (standing): standing in beings

anvaya.base: भूत · being; भावन · causing to be (√भू)
anvaya.parts: भूत (beings) + भावन (who brings into being): one who brings forth beings

verses.explanation: The previous verse revoked in the same breath it was confirmed: beings are in me — and beings are *not* in me. Paśya me yogam aiśvaram: this is not contradiction but the signature of a relation no spatial language can hold; 'in' and 'not in' both fail upward. God's connection to the world is realer than containment — which is why containment-talk must break.
verses.connection: Deliberately fractures 9.4's formula: the truth lives in the tension, not in either half.
verses.reflection: Hold the correction too: not even contained — sovereign. Let God outgrow your best container today.
verses.background: The sovereign paradox is stated: all this world is pervaded by Me; all beings rest in Me — and I am not in them; nor do beings rest in Me. Behold My divine yoga: like wind standing in space, beings stand in Me; nature, under My supervision, produces the moving and unmoving.
verses.hook: What power lets God hold all beings while staying untouched by them?

refs.note: Maya, the material energy, is ashamed even to stand before God, showing how He pervades it yet stays untouched by it.

views.text: The Self is unattached, as the Upaniṣad says, so beings cannot really dwell in it. Calling it "my Self" follows ordinary human usage; it does not mean the Lord thinks his Self is other than himself.
Beings are not held the way a jug holds water; they are held by his will. The divine yoga is that he upholds and controls all beings yet gains nothing from them.
Beings are "not in me" for those blinded by ignorance, who take a finite ego as the basis of knowing. Yoga is the Lord's power, his freedom to act in this wonderfully strange way.
Yoga is the knack of joining what cannot be joined. An embodied soul supports its body and clings to it through ego; the Lord supports and nourishes beings but, having no ego, does not dwell in them.
A third energy, Yogmaya, makes the impossible possible: it hides God though He sits in our hearts, and keeps Him untouched by the material energy He pervades.

verses.devanagari:
यथाकाशस्थितो नित्यं वायुः सर्वत्रगो महान् ।
तथा सर्वाणि भूतानि मत्स्थानीत्युपधारय॥
verses.transliteration:
yathākāśasthito nityaṃ vāyuḥ sarvatrago mahān
tathā sarvāṇi bhūtāni matsthānītyupadhāraya
verses.essence: As the mighty wind, moving everywhere, rests always in space — so, understand, do all beings rest in me.
verses.translation: As the mighty wind, moving everywhere, rests always in the ether, even so, know thou that all beings rest in Me.

anvaya.parts: आकाश (space) + स्थित (situated): situated in space
सर्वत्र (everywhere) + ग (going): going everywhere
मत् (in me) + स्थ (standing): standing in me

anvaya.base: thus (closes what is to be understood)

verses.explanation: The healing image after the fracture: wind in space. Space holds every gust without being pushed by any; the wind moves wildly, the sky it moves through is unmoved, untouched, yet never absent from a single eddy. So beings in him: fully held, never gripping; the holder unstained by the held.
verses.connection: Resolves the 9.4–5 paradox in one simile — intimacy without entanglement.
verses.reflection: Watch wind move through space, owning nothing of it — beings move through Him so. Move so today.
verses.background: The sovereign paradox is stated: all this world is pervaded by Me; all beings rest in Me — and I am not in them; nor do beings rest in Me. Behold My divine yoga: like wind standing in space, beings stand in Me; nature, under My supervision, produces the moving and unmoving.
verses.hook: How do all beings rest in God, like wind in the sky?

views.text: Like the vast wind ever present in space, beings abide in the omnipresent Lord, and they abide there without any contact with him.

The mighty wind moves through space with no visible support, so it must be upheld by the Lord. In the same way all beings are held up by his will alone; scripture says the wind blows from fear of him.
Wind and space go together, yet no one speaks of touching space. So the Absolute pervades the whole universe and still is not grasped by people.
Just as the restless wind never exists apart from the sky, souls moving through countless bodies never exist apart from God, and all creation also rests in Him by depending on His will.

verses.devanagari:
सर्वभूतानि कौन्तेय प्रकृतिं यान्ति मामिकाम् ।
कल्पक्षये पुनस्तानि कल्पादौ विसृजाम्यहम्॥
verses.transliteration:
sarvabhūtāni kaunteya prakṛtiṃ yānti māmikām
kalpakṣaye punastāni kalpādau visṛjāmyaham
verses.essence: All beings, Kaunteya, enter my nature at the end of a cosmic cycle; at the beginning of the next cycle, I send them forth again.
verses.translation: All beings, O Arjuna, go into My Nature at the end of a Kalpa; I send them forth again at the beginning of (the next) Kalpa.

anvaya.parts: सर्व (all) + भूत (beings): all beings

anvaya.meaning: at the end of a kalpa
anvaya.base: कल्प · cosmic age; क्षय · end, decay
anvaya.parts: कल्प (cosmic age) + क्षय (end): the end of a cosmic age

anvaya.meaning: at the start of a kalpa
anvaya.parts: कल्प (cosmic age) + आदि (beginning): the beginning of a cosmic age

verses.explanation: The breathing cosmos of chapter 8, now in the first person: at the great evening, beings fold into *my* nature; at the great morning, *I* release them. The cycle has acquired an owner and a will. What looked like impersonal tide from outside is, from his side, deliberate exhalation and welcome home.
verses.connection: Re-states 8.18–19's dissolution-and-emergence with the pronoun that changes its meaning.
verses.reflection: Let one ending today be an in-breath, not a verdict — all beings return to be breathed out again.
verses.background: The sovereign paradox is stated: all this world is pervaded by Me; all beings rest in Me — and I am not in them; nor do beings rest in Me. Behold My divine yoga: like wind standing in space, beings stand in Me; nature, under My supervision, produces the moving and unmoving.
verses.hook: Where do all beings go when the universe dissolves?

views.text: The nature beings return to is the Lord's lower prakṛti of the three guṇas; from it he projects them again as in earlier cycles.
Prakṛti is the Lord's body, called Tamas when it cannot be told apart by name and form. Beings enter it at the end of Brahmā's life by his will, and he sends the same beings forth again.
"Nature" here means the Lord's unmanifest form.
At the end of Brahma's life the elements merge back step by step into primal matter, which rests in God; souls rest there too with only causal bodies until creation unfolds again.

verses.devanagari:
प्रकृतिं स्वामवष्टभ्य विसृजामि पुनः पुनः ।
भूतग्राममिमं कृत्स्नमवशं प्रकृतेर्वशात्॥
verses.transliteration:
prakṛtiṃ svāmavaṣṭabhya visṛjāmi punaḥ punaḥ
bhūtagrāmamimaṃ kṛtsnamavaśaṃ prakṛtervaśāt
verses.essence: Taking hold of my own nature, I send forth again and again this whole host of beings — helpless under nature's sway.
verses.translation: Animating My Nature, I again and again send forth all this multitude of beings, helpless by the force of the Nature.

anvaya.parts: भूत (beings) + ग्राम (multitude): the multitude of beings
अ (without) + वश (control): having no control

verses.explanation: The mechanics of the great morning: he leans on his nature (avaṣṭabhya — as a king leans on an instrument) and the multitude streams out, avaśam, not by their choice but by the momentum of their own unfinished karma. Creation is thus both his act and their necessity: he opens the door; their unspent tendencies walk them through it.
verses.connection: Details 9.7's sending-forth — and quietly explains why beings return at all: unfinished business.
verses.reflection: Feel nature's helpless reissuing in your own habits — and the freedom of the one presiding over them.
verses.background: The sovereign paradox is stated: all this world is pervaded by Me; all beings rest in Me — and I am not in them; nor do beings rest in Me. Behold My divine yoga: like wind standing in space, beings stand in Me; nature, under My supervision, produces the moving and unmoving.
verses.hook: Why are beings brought forth again and again, cycle after cycle?

views.text: The prakṛti he controls is nescience. Beings are powerless because ignorance and other defects keep them subject to their own nature.
He develops his wonderfully potent prakṛti eightfold and sends forth the fourfold host of gods, animals, humans and immobile things, all held by the deluding guṇas.
Taking hold of his own nature means that this host of beings, insentient in itself, gains luminosity by being linked to the Absolute's nature as consciousness.
"By the force of nature" means by the strength of each being's own disposition, shaped by its past karma; the beings dissolved at the end of the age are created again in their variety.
When creation unfolds again, souls held in suspended animation are placed back in the world and receive subtle and gross bodies according to their causal bodies, forming the many kinds of life.

verses.devanagari:
न च मां तानि कर्माणि निबध्नन्ति धनञ्जय ।
उदासीनवदासीनमसक्तं तेषु कर्मसु॥
verses.transliteration:
na ca māṃ tāni karmāṇi nibadhnanti dhanañjaya
udāsīnavadāsīnamasaktaṃ teṣu karmasu
verses.essence: Nor do these actions bind me, Dhananjaya — seated as one indifferent, unattached to those acts.
verses.translation: These acts do not bind Me, O Arjuna, sitting like one indifferent, unattached to those acts.

anvaya.parts: धन (wealth) + जय (winning): one who wins wealth
उदासीन (neutral onlooker) + वत् (like): like a neutral onlooker

anvaya.form: present participle, masculine, accusative singular (describing me)

anvaya.parts: अ (not) + सक्त (attached): not attached

verses.explanation: The Creator audits his own karma and finds none accruing: udāsīna-vat, *as if* uninvolved — the work happens, vast beyond counting, with no craving in the worker. This is chapter 4's secret (action without bondage) demonstrated at maximum scale: if universes can be issued without attachment, an arrow can be loosed without it.
verses.connection: The divine proof-of-concept for everything taught to Arjuna about unbinding action.
verses.reflection: Do one task today seated as if indifferent — fully acting, unattached, the way worlds are made.
verses.background: The sovereign paradox is stated: all this world is pervaded by Me; all beings rest in Me — and I am not in them; nor do beings rest in Me. Behold My divine yoga: like wind standing in space, beings stand in Me; nature, under My supervision, produces the moving and unmoving.
verses.hook: Why do the acts of creation not bind God?

refs.note: The material energy is inert by itself and acts as if alive only when God inspires it, explaining how creation proceeds while He stays unaffected.

views.text: What frees the Lord is the absence of the ego-sense "I do" and of attachment to results; the same holds for anyone. Without them a foolish person is bound by his own actions, like a silkworm in its cocoon.
The unequal conditions of creation come from the beings' own past karma, so no cruelty or partiality can be charged to the Lord; the Brahma Sūtras answer the same objection.
Attachment is what binds, and the Lord has it not, since all his desires are fulfilled. He says "like" one indifferent, because someone truly indifferent could not be an agent at all.
Inert matter works only when God animates it, like tongs in a cook's hand; yet He stays blissful and untouched by its work, needing nothing outside Himself.

verses.devanagari:
मयाध्यक्षेण प्रकृतिः सूयते सचराचरम् ।
हेतुनानेन कौन्तेय जगद्विपरिवर्तते॥
verses.transliteration:
mayādhyakṣeṇa prakṛtiḥ sūyate sacarācaram
hetunānena kaunteya jagadviparivartate
verses.essence: Under my supervision, nature brings forth the moving and the unmoving. By this cause, Kaunteya, the world revolves.
verses.translation: Under Me as supervisor, Nature produces the moving and the unmoving; because of this, O Arjuna, the world revolves.

anvaya.parts: अधि (over) + अक्ष (eye): one who watches over
स (with) + चर (moving) + अचर (unmoving): all that moves and does not move

verses.explanation: The division of labor stated cleanly: prakṛti does the producing; he presides — adhyakṣeṇa, as the overseeing presence whose mere witness sets the whole factory in motion, the way the sun farms nothing yet ripens everything. Power exercised as presidency, not as labor: the world turns because it is watched.
verses.connection: Completes 9.7–9's cosmology: nature the engine, the Lord its still ignition.
verses.reflection: Remember once today who supervises the machinery — and let prakriti handle the machinery part.
verses.background: The sovereign paradox is stated: all this world is pervaded by Me; all beings rest in Me — and I am not in them; nor do beings rest in Me. Behold My divine yoga: like wind standing in space, beings stand in Me; nature, under My supervision, produces the moving and unmoving.
verses.hook: If nature does the producing, in what sense is God the creator?

views.text: Adhyakṣa means the changeless mere witness. Every activity of the world exists in, and ends in, the one witnessing consciousness, so the question "why was the world created?" has no real ground.
Prakṛti creates because the Lord looks at it through his will, and it creates in keeping with each soul's karma; this shows his sovereignty and his freedom from cruelty.
He presides by mere proximity, so being the agent of creation and remaining indifferent do not conflict.
God does not create directly; His energies and appointed beings such as Brahma do the work under His sanction, just as a head of state is credited with what his officials do.

verses.devanagari:
अवजानन्ति मां मूढा मानुषीं तनुमाश्रितम् ।
परं भावमजानन्तो मम भूतमहेश्वरम्॥
verses.transliteration:
avajānanti māṃ mūḍhā mānuṣīṃ tanumāśritam
paraṃ bhāvamajānanto mama bhūtamaheśvaram
verses.essence: The deluded disregard me when I dwell in human form — not knowing my higher being as the great Lord of all that is.
verses.translation: Fools disregard Me, clad in human form, not knowing My higher Being as the great Lord of (all) beings.

anvaya.form: past participle used as noun, masculine, nominative plural (subject)

anvaya.base: आ + √श्रि · to resort to, take on
anvaya.form: past participle, masculine, accusative singular (describing me)
present participle, negated, masculine, nominative plural

anvaya.parts: भूत (beings) + महा (great) + ईश्वर (lord): the great Lord of all beings

verses.explanation: The cost of the camouflage: avajānanti — they look down on him, the overseer of 9.10, because he stands beside them wearing skin. It is the permanent scandal of incarnation: the infinite made approachable is mistaken for merely ordinary. Familiarity, which should have been the gift, becomes the veil.
verses.connection: The shadow of divine nearness: what 7.24–25 warned about, witnessed on the ground.
verses.reflection: Catch yourself disregarding the divine in human dress today — the ordinary form is the disguise.
verses.background: Krishna names the great mistake and its opposite: fools disregard Me dwelling in human form, not knowing My higher being — while the great souls, sheltered in the divine nature, worship with undistracted mind, ever singing, striving, bowing.
verses.hook: Why do some people fail to recognize the divine in human form?

refs.note: Describes the Lord with a forest garland playing His flute, showing scripture speaks of God's personal form.
A seer reports seeing God as an imperishable boy among cowherds, supporting the verse's point that He takes a human-like form.
The deepest knowledge is that the Supreme takes a human-like form, which the deluded of this verse fail to see.

views.text: His supreme nature is subtler and more pervasive than space, the Self of all beings. Fools belittle him when he acts through a human body, and that constant disrespect ruins them.
The higher nature they miss is his compassion, generosity and parental care, the very reason he took a human form to be everyone's refuge; seeing the form, they take him for a man like themselves.
Because he is the Self of all, lying within everything born, people ask how a Lord could exist apart from the creatures they see, and so they disrespect him.
His body is made of pure sattva, taken on in human shape at his devotees' wish; that human appearance is exactly what gives the deluded their excuse for contempt.
Denying God a personal form makes Him less than complete; His form is divine, eternal and blissful, and souls with material eyes may have seen Him on earth without recognizing Him.

verses.devanagari:
मोघाशा मोघकर्माणो मोघज्ञाना विचेतसः ।
राक्षसीमासुरीं चैव प्रकृतिं मोहिनीं श्रिताः॥
verses.transliteration:
moghāśā moghakarmāṇo moghajñānā vicetasaḥ
rākṣasīmāsurīṃ caiva prakṛtiṃ mohinīṃ śritāḥ
verses.essence: Of vain hopes, vain works, vain knowledge, devoid of sense — they take on the deluding nature of fiends and demons.
verses.translation: Of vain hopes, of vain actions, of vain knowledge and senseless, they verily are possessed of the deceitful nature of demons and undivine beings.

anvaya.parts: मोघ (vain) + आशा (hope): those whose hopes are vain
मोघ (vain) + कर्मन् (action): those whose actions are vain
मोघ (vain) + ज्ञान (knowledge): those whose knowledge is vain
वि (without, astray) + चेतस् (mind): those whose mind has gone astray

verses.explanation: Where the disregard of 9.11 leads: mogha three times — hopes, works, knowledge, all running on empty, because a life mis-sourced at the root mis-fires in every branch. To miss the divine in the world's center is not one error among many; it is the error that hollows out all the others.
verses.connection: Traces 9.11's contempt to its harvest: a whole existence gone mogha, futile.
verses.reflection: Check your hopes, works, and knowledge for vanity once today — empty things keep busy schedules.
verses.background: Krishna names the great mistake and its opposite: fools disregard Me dwelling in human form, not knowing My higher being — while the great souls, sheltered in the divine nature, worship with undistracted mind, ever singing, striving, bowing.
verses.hook: What becomes of the hopes and knowledge of those who deny the divine?

views.text: Even their rites such as the Agnihotra bear no fruit, because they disregard the Lord who is their own Self. The fiendish and demonic nature is the belief that the body is the Self, which breeds cruelty and theft.
Their action, knowledge and aspiration are futile because all of them are aimed at the unreal; the two natures are excessive desire and ignorance.

Their hope is vain because they expect another deity to reward them faster; their works fail because they turn from the Lord. The fiendish nature is tamasic and violent, the demonic rajasic, full of lust and pride.

Theories that reduce Krishna to a yogi, a lesser deity or worse come from minds deluded by matter; without devotion to His personal form, and unable to worship the formless, their hopes for lasting welfare fail.

verses.devanagari:
महात्मानस्तु मां पार्थ दैवीं प्रकृतिमाश्रिताः ।
भजन्त्यनन्यमनसो ज्ञात्वा भूतादिमव्ययम्॥
verses.transliteration:
mahātmānastu māṃ pārtha daivīṃ prakṛtimāśritāḥ
bhajantyananyamanaso jñātvā bhūtādimavyayam
verses.essence: But the great souls, Partha, sheltered in the divine nature, worship me with undistracted mind — knowing me as the imperishable origin of beings.
verses.translation: But the great souls, O Arjuna, partaking of My divine nature, worship Me with a single mind (with the mind devoted to nothing else), knowing Me as the imperishable source of beings.

anvaya.parts: महा (great) + आत्मन् (self): those whose self is great
अनन्य (no other) + मनस् (mind): whose mind goes to no other
भूत (beings) + आदि (origin): the origin of all beings

verses.explanation: The counter-portrait: same human form before them, opposite recognition. The mahātmās see through the skin to the bhūtādi, the origin of all that is, and their response is ananya-manasaḥ — attention without a second address. Greatness of soul, in this chapter's ledger, is measured purely by accuracy of recognition.
verses.connection: The fork from 9.11–12: two kinds of people, distinguished only by what they see in the same place.
verses.reflection: Borrow the mahatma's posture for an hour: sheltered in the divine nature, knowing the Imperishable source.
verses.background: Krishna names the great mistake and its opposite: fools disregard Me dwelling in human form, not knowing My higher being — while the great souls, sheltered in the divine nature, worship with undistracted mind, ever singing, striving, bowing.
verses.hook: How do great souls relate to God, unlike the deluded?

refs.note: Radha appears as Lakshmi, Rukmini, Sita and others, showing the one divine energy in many forms, which great souls take shelter of.

views.text: The divine nature means self-control, kindness and faith. Bhūtādi is the source of the elements, beginning with space, as well as of living beings.
Freed from evil by many good acts, they grasp that the Lord came in human form out of compassion. He is so dear to them that without worshipping him their mind and senses find no support.
The divine nature is the one listed later, beginning with fearlessness and purity of heart; the great-souled are those whose minds desire has not overpowered.
Great souls have woken from the dream of material life and live under God's divine energy, Yogmaya, whose grace brings them love and knowledge of God and uninterrupted devotion.

verses.devanagari:
सततं कीर्तयन्तो मां यतन्तश्च दृढव्रताः ।
नमस्यन्तश्च मां भक्त्या नित्ययुक्ता उपासते॥
verses.transliteration:
satataṃ kīrtayanto māṃ yatantaśca dṛḍhavratāḥ
namasyantaśca māṃ bhaktyā nityayuktā upāsate
verses.essence: Ever glorifying me and striving with firm vows, bowing to me in devotion — always harnessed, they worship me.
verses.translation: Always glorifying Me, striving,firm in vows, prostrating themselves before Me, they worship Me with devotion always steadfast.

anvaya.parts: दृढ (firm) + व्रत (vow): whose vows are firm
नित्य (always) + युक्त (joined): always joined in yoga

verses.explanation: The texture of the great souls' days: kīrtana, the spilling-over of love into song and speech; effort held by vows; the body folded in namas. Note that worship here is continuous tense throughout — satatam, nitya — not an appointment kept but a current lived in. Devotion as climate, not weather.
verses.connection: Shows 9.13's recognition in practice — the daily liturgy of those who see.
verses.reflection: Keep one small vow firmly today and bow once inwardly — perpetual yoking is built of such bricks.
verses.background: Krishna names the great mistake and its opposite: fools disregard Me dwelling in human form, not knowing My higher being — while the great souls, sheltered in the divine nature, worship with undistracted mind, ever singing, striving, bowing.
verses.hook: What do devoted people actually do in their worship?

refs.note: Each age has its best practice, and in the present age it is chanting God's glories, supporting the verse's picture of devotees who always glorify Him.
In this age, singing God's glories is the one way to cross the ocean of worldly existence.
Defines kīrtan as singing aloud the names, forms, qualities and pastimes of God.

views.text: Striving means effort through withdrawal of the senses, self-control, kindness and non-injury; the bowing is to the Lord as the Self dwelling in the heart.
They cannot bear a moment without him: they call out Nārāyaṇa, Kṛṣṇa, Vāsudeva with trembling voices, work for temples and gardens, and fall in full prostration, longing for eternal service.
Three groups are described: some sing his praises, some strive in vows and worship, others bow in devotion; "ever united" and "with devotion" apply to all three.
Devotees practise through kīrtan, which joins hearing, chanting and remembering; it keeps the restless mind returning to God, drives away sleep and suits groups, so saints have favoured it most.

verses.devanagari:
ज्ञानयज्ञेन चाप्यन्ये यजन्तो मामुपासते ।
एकत्वेन पृथक्त्वेन बहुधा विश्वतोमुखम्॥
verses.transliteration:
jñānayajñena cāpyanye yajanto māmupāsate
ekatvena pṛthaktvena bahudhā viśvatomukham
verses.essence: Others, sacrificing with the sacrifice of knowledge, worship me as the One, as the distinct, as the manifold — me, facing every direction.
verses.translation: Others also sacrificing with the wisdom-sacrifice worship Me, the All-faced, as one, as distinct, and as manifold.

anvaya.parts: ज्ञान (knowledge) + यज्ञ (sacrifice): the sacrifice that is knowledge

anvaya.form: noun, neuter, instrumental singular (by way of)
noun, neuter, instrumental singular (by way of)

anvaya.base: विश्वतस् · on all sides; मुख · face
anvaya.parts: विश्वतः (on all sides) + मुख (face): whose face is everywhere

verses.explanation: The philosophers' worship admitted alongside the singers': some adore him as the One without second, some as the Other to be loved across a sacred distance, some as the many faces of the world itself. Viśvato-mukham — facing all ways — he receives every metaphysics as a mode of approach. The map wars are his to smile at; all the maps are of him.
verses.connection: Extends 9.14's devotion to its intellectual forms — monist, dualist, pluralist, all counted as yajna.
verses.reflection: Worship by your own grain today — as one, as distinct, as the all-faced — every geometry is received.
verses.background: Krishna names the great mistake and its opposite: fools disregard Me dwelling in human form, not knowing My higher being — while the great souls, sheltered in the divine nature, worship with undistracted mind, ever singing, striving, bowing.
verses.hook: How do those on the path of knowledge worship God?

views.text: The sacrifice is the knowledge that Brahman is one. Others worship him separately as the sun, moon and so on, and others as the Cosmic Person whose face is everywhere.
They contemplate one Lord who has all beings as his modes and the whole cosmos as his body: one as the bearer of the modes, many in the forms he takes.
Some worship him through knowledge alone as the One; others through external sacrifice and the yoga of action as the Many. Both take him as their highest goal.
Oneness is meditating that only the supreme Brahman exists; separateness is the attitude "I am his servant"; the manifold way is worshipping him as Brahmā, Rudra and the other gods.

Seekers approach God differently: the path of knowledge worships His formless aspect, some see themselves as distinct from Him, others worship the universe as God, a view that is right but incomplete.

verses.devanagari:
अहं क्रतुरहं यज्ञः स्वधाहमहमौषधम् ।
मन्त्रोऽहमहमेवाज्यमहमग्निरहं हुतम्॥
verses.transliteration:
ahaṃ kraturahaṃ yajñaḥ svadhāhamahamauṣadham
mantro'hamahamevājyamahamagnirahaṃ hutam
verses.essence: I am the rite, I am the sacrifice, I am the offering to the ancestors, I am the herb; I am the mantra, I the clarified butter, I the fire, I the oblation.
verses.translation: I am the Kratu; I am the Yajna; I am the offering (food) to the manes; I am the medicinal herbs and all the plants; I am the Mantra; I am also the Ghee or the melted butter; I am the fire; I am the oblation.

anvaya.form: past participle used as noun, neuter, nominative singular

verses.explanation: The 'I am' litany begins, and its first sweep claims the whole apparatus of religion: the ritual, its words, its butter and flame and the very act of pouring. Worship, analyzed, contains no ingredient that is not him — the worshiped, yes, but also the worship. He is on both sides of every altar.
verses.connection: Opens the great self-declaration (9.16–19), echoing 4.24's Brahman-in-every-element at full voice.
verses.reflection: Find Him in the verbs of your day once: the offering, the fire, the act of offering itself.
verses.background: The voice of the Lord annexes the entire ritual cosmos in first person: I am the rite, the sacrifice, the offering, the herb, the mantra, the fire; father, mother, grandsire of the world; the goal, the witness, the abode, the friend; heat, rain, immortality and death, being and non-being.
verses.hook: What does God say He is within the ritual of sacrifice?

refs.note: God manifested the Vedas through His breath, so the sacred knowledge used in sacrifice is part of Him.

views.text: Kratu is a Vedic (śrauta) rite and yajña a sacrifice prescribed by the Smṛtis; auṣadha is either the food all creatures eat or medicine for disease.
Kratu means rites like the Jyotiṣṭoma, yajña the five great daily sacrifices, and the herb stands for the oblation itself; the list is meant to cover every part of worship.
Krishna offers a glimpse of His infinite personality: every part of the sacrifice, from the ritual and the herbs to the fire and the offering, is an aspect of Him.

verses.devanagari:
पिताहमस्य जगतो माता धाता पितामहः ।
वेद्यं पवित्रमोंकार ऋक्साम यजुरेव च॥
verses.transliteration:
pitāhamasya jagato mātā dhātā pitāmahaḥ
vedyaṃ pavitramoṃkāra ṛksāma yajureva ca
verses.essence: I am the father of this universe, the mother, the sustainer, the grandsire; the object of knowledge, the purifier, the syllable Om; the Rik, the Sama and the Yajus.
verses.translation: I am the father of this world, the mother, the dispenser of the fruits of actions and the grandfather; the (one) thing to be known, the purifier, the sacred monosyllable (Om), and also the Rik-, the Sama-and the Yajur-Vedas.

anvaya.form: gerundive (to be known), neuter, nominative singular

anvaya.parts: ओम् (Om) + कार (the sound): the sound Om

anvaya.base: ऋच् · Vedic verse, the Ṛg Veda
यजुस् · sacrificial formula, the Yajur Veda

verses.explanation: From ritual to family: pitā, mātā — and mother is no afterthought; the universe is parented from both sides by the same One. Then lineage stretches back (grandsire) and scripture itself folds in: the three Vedas are not about him; they are him, the way a person's voice is the person.
verses.connection: The litany turns intimate: cosmos as household, with God at every kinship position.
verses.reflection: Address the universe familially once today: father, mother, grandsire — and feel the cosmos warm.
verses.background: The voice of the Lord annexes the entire ritual cosmos in first person: I am the rite, the sacrifice, the offering, the herb, the mantra, the fire; father, mother, grandsire of the world; the goal, the witness, the abode, the friend; heat, rain, immortality and death, being and non-being.
verses.hook: In what relationships does God stand to this whole world?

refs.note: God manifested the Vedas through His breath, which is why He can say He is the Vedas themselves.

views.text: Dhātā is the dispenser of the results of actions. The knowable Brahman is reached through Om, on which the three Vedas are the authority, and "and" hints at the Atharva Veda too.
Dhātṛ is someone other than the parents who helps bring a person to birth. Om is named as the source of knowledge and the seed of the Vedas.
Īśvara is the father, primordial Nature the mother, and the pure Existence-Knowledge-Bliss Absolute the grandfather.
Creation comes from God, so He is its father; He holds matter in His womb before creation, so its mother; He sustains it, and as Brahma's father He is its grandfather.

verses.devanagari:
गतिर्भर्ता प्रभुः साक्षी निवासः शरणं सुहृत् ।
प्रभवः प्रलयः स्थानं निधानं बीजमव्ययम्॥
verses.transliteration:
gatirbhartā prabhuḥ sākṣī nivāsaḥ śaraṇaṃ suhṛt
prabhavaḥ pralayaḥ sthānaṃ nidhānaṃ bījamavyayam
verses.essence: I am the goal, the sustainer, the lord, the witness, the abode, the refuge, the friend; the origin, the dissolution, the foundation, the treasury, the imperishable seed.
verses.translation: I am the goal, the supporter, the Lord, the witness, the abode, the shelter, the friend, the origin, the dissolution, the foundation, the treasure-house and the seed which is imperishable.

anvaya.parts: सु (good) + हृद् (heart): the good-hearted one

verses.explanation: Twelve names in two lines, and buried among the cosmic titles, one small word glows: suhṛt — friend, the well-wisher who needs no reason (5.29's word returning). The verse sweeps from gatiḥ, the destination of all journeys, to bījam avyayam, the seed never spent — and insists the same One is also simply *on your side*.
verses.connection: Continues 9.16–17's roll-call from functions to relationships — power that is also companionship.
verses.reflection: Pick one of the twelve names for your need today — refuge, friend, witness, abode — and use it.
verses.background: The voice of the Lord annexes the entire ritual cosmos in first person: I am the rite, the sacrifice, the offering, the herb, the mantra, the fire; father, mother, grandsire of the world; the goal, the witness, the abode, the friend; heat, rain, immortality and death, being and non-being.
verses.hook: Who is your lasting refuge, friend and final destination?

refs.note: Lord Narayan alone is the soul's mother, father, beloved and destination, echoing this verse's list of God as refuge and friend.
A devotee tells Lord Ram that He alone is his master and the knower of his heart.

views.text: Gati is the fruit of action, the treasure-house is what beings will enjoy in future, and the seed is imperishable because creation never stops and nothing sprouts without a seed.
Gati is the place to be reached from everywhere; refuge is the conscious one sought because he brings what is good and removes what is harmful; friend is one who wishes well.
Nidhāna is the place where all is laid to rest in dissolution, and the seed is imperishable, unlike a grain of rice that is used up when it sprouts.
Bodily relations are temporary and self-interested, but God has accompanied the soul through every birth and loves it selflessly, so He alone is the soul's true father, mother and friend.

verses.devanagari:
तपाम्यहमहं वर्षं निगृह्णाम्युत्सृजामि च ।
अमृतं चैव मृत्युश्च सदसच्चाहमर्जुन॥
verses.transliteration:
tapāmyahamahaṃ varṣaṃ nigṛhṇāmyutsṛjāmi ca
amṛtaṃ caiva mṛtyuśca sadasaccāhamarjuna
verses.essence: I give heat; I withhold and send forth the rain. I am immortality and also death; being and non-being am I, Arjuna.
verses.translation: (As the sun) I give heat; I withhold and send forth the rain; I am immortality and also death, existence and non-existence, O Arjuna.

anvaya.parts: अ (not) + मृत (dead): the deathless

anvaya.base: सत् · being, the existent (√अस् · to be)

anvaya.parts: अ (not) + सत् (being): what is not manifest

verses.explanation: The litany ends by refusing every flattering edit: not only sun and rain but the withholding of rain; not only amṛta but mṛtyu, death itself; sat *and* asat. A God who owned only the pleasant column would be half a God and no refuge in the dark. This completeness is the chapter's severest comfort: nothing that happens, happens outside him.
verses.connection: Closes the self-declaration at full span — both poles of every pair, claimed.
verses.reflection: Bless both weathers today: the heat and the rain, the holding back and the sending forth.
verses.background: The voice of the Lord annexes the entire ritual cosmos in first person: I am the rite, the sacrifice, the offering, the herb, the mantra, the fire; father, mother, grandsire of the world; the goal, the witness, the abode, the friend; heat, rain, immortality and death, being and non-being.
verses.hook: Is God both life and death, being and non-being?

refs.note: God tells Brahma that He alone existed before creation, is all that now exists, and remains after dissolution, supporting the verse's claim that He is both being and non-being.

views.text: As the sun he heats, pours rain and draws it back. Sat is the manifest effect and asat its unmanifest cause; neither is absolutely real or absolutely nothing, and the Lord is never mere non-existence.
Being is what exists now; non-being is what existed before or may exist later. All things in every state are his body and modes, so he alone exists.
The whole litany teaches the one Brahman without parts: action done knowing that all its factors are the Self does not bind but leads to the Lord.
Since God is all that exists, even the material we worship Him with is Him; what pleases Him is not the offering itself but the love behind it.

verses.devanagari:
त्रैविद्या मां सोमपाः पूतपापा
यज्ञैरिष्ट्वा स्वर्गतिं प्रार्थयन्ते ।
ते पुण्यमासाद्य सुरेन्द्रलोक-
मश्नन्ति दिव्यान्दिवि देवभोगान्॥
verses.transliteration:
traividyā māṃ somapāḥ pūtapāpā yajñairiṣṭvā svargatiṃ prārthayante
te puṇyamāsādya surendralokamaśnanti divyāndivi devabhogān
verses.essence: The knowers of the three Vedas, soma-drinkers cleansed of sin, worship me with sacrifice seeking heaven; reaching Indra's holy world, they taste the gods' celestial pleasures.
verses.translation: The knowers of the three Vedas, the drinkers of Soma, purified of all sins, worshipping Me by sacrifices, pray for the way to heaven; they reach the holy world of the Lord of the gods and enjoy in heaven the divine pleasures of the gods.

सोम (soma juice) + पा (drinking): those who drink soma

स्वर् (heaven) + गति (going, goal): the goal that is heaven

verses.explanation: The orthodox high-achievers get their due: ritual mastered, sins washed, heaven won — the system works exactly as advertised. The verse withholds all sarcasm; the soma-drinkers truly arrive at Indra's banquet. The audit comes next, and it concerns not the prize's reality but its battery life.
verses.connection: Begins the heaven-economics passage (9.20–21): merit's genuine, finite returns.
verses.reflection: Watch a reward expire today — pleasure ending on schedule — and want the unexpiring a little more.
verses.background: Krishna audits religion itself: the Veda-knowers who drink soma reach heaven and, merit spent, return — coming and going, ruled by desire. But for those who think of Me with no other thought, I carry what they lack and preserve what they have; worshipers reach what they worship — My devotees come to Me.
verses.hook: What do those who worship through Vedic rituals for heaven attain?

views.text: These ritualists are 'ignorant and desirous of pleasures'; the 'Me' they worship is the Lord appearing in the forms of the Vasus and other gods, and the holy world they reach is simply the fruit of merit.
Followers of the three Vedas are set apart from those who rely on Vedanta: in honouring Indra they really worship the Lord, but they do not know he abides in those gods, so they ask only for heaven.
Read as a warning to aspirants: celestial beings flatter the advancing yogi with heavenly comforts, and the unwary one mistakes them for the goal and loses discrimination.
Ritualists who worship the celestial gods are neither atheists nor devotees; they worship God only indirectly, and their good deeds win heavenly pleasures but no release from birth and death.

verses.devanagari:

verses.translation: They, having enjoyed the vast heaven, enter the world of mortals when their merit is exhausted; thus abiding by the injunctions of the three (Vedas) and desiring (objects of) desires, they attain to the state of going and returning.

verses.explanation: The battery dies: kṣīṇe puṇye — merit, being earned, is spendable, and heaven runs on it like a meter. Then the re-entry, and the chapter's most economical phrase for samsara: gatāgatam, going-and-coming, the commute of souls. Desiring desires (kāma-kāmāḥ), they receive exactly that — desire's infinite installment plan.
verses.connection: The expiry-date on 9.20's prize, setting up the contrast of 9.22's unmetered care.
verses.reflection: Stop commuting between earning and spending merit; ask today for what does not run out.
verses.background: Krishna audits religion itself: the Veda-knowers who drink soma reach heaven and, merit spent, return — coming and going, ruled by desire. But for those who think of Me with no other thought, I carry what they lack and preserve what they have; worshipers reach what they worship — My devotees come to Me.
verses.hook: What happens after the pleasures of heaven are used up?

refs.note: Heaven's residents enjoy only until their merit is spent, then time forces them to fall, as this verse describes.
Heaven is brief and ends in suffering.
Human birth is so rare that even the gods pray for it, so it should be used to seek God rather than heaven.

views.text: The point of 'only' going and returning: Vedic ritual alone wins them a round trip, never independence.
The trifling, transient pleasures of heaven are set against the great souls who meditate on the Lord, reach boundless bliss and do not return to samsara.
They do worship Vasudeva alone; it is their own weakness that ties the act to heaven as its only result. Rebirth is not the inherent nature of sacrifice itself.
Heaven is temporary and every soul has been there many times; only human birth allows God-realization, so instead of seeking heaven one should seek God through devotion.

अनन्याश्चिन्तयन्तो मां ये जनाः पर्युपासते ।
तेषां नित्याभियुक्तानां योगक्षेमं वहाम्यहम्॥
verses.transliteration:
ananyāścintayanto māṃ ye janāḥ paryupāsate
teṣāṃ nityābhiyuktānāṃ yogakṣemaṃ vahāmyaham
verses.essence: For those who worship me thinking of nothing else, ever harnessed — I carry what they lack, and I preserve what they have.
verses.translation: For those men who worship Me alone, thinking of no other, for those ever-united, I secure what is not already possessed and preserve what they already possess.

anvaya.form: adjective, masculine, nominative plural (describing the subject)
anvaya.parts: अन् (not) + अन्य (other): those who have no other

anvaya.form: relative pronoun, masculine, nominative plural (those who)

anvaya.base: परि + उप + √आस् · to sit near, worship

anvaya.parts: नित्य (always) + अभियुक्त (engaged, intent): those always engaged in me
योग (getting what is lacking) + क्षेम (keeping what is had): the pair taken as one

verses.explanation: The chapter's most cherished sentence turns on one verb: vahāmi, *I carry* — not 'arrange', not 'grant', but shoulder, personally, like a porter. Yoga is the obtaining of what is lacking, kṣema the guarding of what is held; together they are the entire economy of anxiety, and he takes over both departments for whoever stops dividing their attention. The contract has one clause: ananyāḥ, no second object. It is the Gita's most audacious promise of providence: the Lord making himself the devotee's servant of logistics.
verses.connection: The answer to 9.21's metered heaven: undivided devotion is the one account he funds himself.
verses.reflection: Give Him your undivided hour and let Him carry the logistics — yoga-kshemam vahamy aham. Test it.
verses.background: Krishna audits religion itself: the Veda-knowers who drink soma reach heaven and, merit spent, return — coming and going, ruled by desire. But for those who think of Me with no other thought, I carry what they lack and preserve what they have; worshipers reach what they worship — My devotees come to Me.
verses.hook: Who takes care of those who depend on God completely?

views.text: Ananyāḥ means 'not different from me': monks who know the Lord as their own Self. He provides for all devotees, but these alone make no effort for themselves, so he carries their needs entirely.
Yoga is the Lord bringing such devotees to himself, kṣema keeping them there for ever; the promise means they never return to samsara.
Yoga is realising the Lord's nature not realised before; kṣema is guarding that realisation, so there is not even a doubt of falling from yoga.
Yoga is gaining wealth and the like, kṣema its protection, or else liberation; the Lord carries these to his single-minded devotees even when they do not ask.
Like a mother with a newborn, God personally supplies what devoted souls lack and protects what they have, but only in proportion to their surrender; to those wholly dependent He gives full care.

te'pi māmeva kaunteya yajantyavidhipūrvakam
verses.essence: Even those devoted to other gods, who sacrifice to them filled with faith — they too worship me alone, Kaunteya, though not according to the rule.
verses.translation: Even those devotees who, endowed with faith, worship other gods, worship Me alone, O Arjuna, b the wrong method.

anvaya.form: relative pronoun, masculine, nominative plural (those who)

anvaya.parts: अन्य (other) + देवता (deity) + भक्त (devoted): those devoted to other deities

verses.explanation: The widest net in the chapter: every faithful offering at every altar lands, in fact, on his table — te 'pi mām eva. The qualifier avidhi-pūrvakam, 'not by the proper rule,' is gentle: not wrong worship but worship with an incomplete address, a letter that arrives because the postmaster knows for whom it was really meant.
verses.connection: Reaffirms 7.21–22 inside the royal teaching: all faith routes to one receiver.
verses.reflection: Honor every sincere worship you see today — it reaches Him, though the address be approximate.
verses.background: Krishna audits religion itself: the Veda-knowers who drink soma reach heaven and, merit spent, return — coming and going, ruled by desire. But for those who think of Me with no other thought, I carry what they lack and preserve what they have; worshipers reach what they worship — My devotees come to Me.
verses.hook: Whom are people really worshipping when they worship other gods?

refs.note: Watering a tree's root nourishes the whole tree, so worshipping the Supreme satisfies all the gods, while worshipping them alone misses the root.

views.text: 'Not by the rule' means in ignorance: they worship the one Lord without knowing it is he they worship.
All beings are the Lord's body and he is their self, so names like Indra finally denote him; the flaw is worshipping the deities without knowing their place as his body.
Avidhi should not be read as 'defective rite' but as 'by different injunctions': nothing is worshipped apart from Brahman, and the commentator rebukes those who insult other systems.
It is true they worship the Lord, but without the rite that leads to liberation, which is why they come back.
Worship of the celestial gods reaches God indirectly, since their powers come from Him, but it is like watering leaves instead of roots: it brings material favours without spiritual benefit.

verses.devanagari:
अहं हि सर्वयज्ञानां भोक्ता च प्रभुरेव च ।
न तु मामभिजानन्ति तत्त्वेनातश्च्यवन्ति ते॥
verses.transliteration:
ahaṃ hi sarvayajñānāṃ bhoktā ca prabhureva ca
na tu māmabhijānanti tattvenātaścyavanti te
verses.essence: For I am the enjoyer and the lord of all sacrifices. But they do not know me in truth — and so they fall back.
verses.translation: (For) I alone am the enjoyer and also the Lord of all sacrifices; but they do not know Me in essence (in reality), and hence they fall (return to this mortal world).

anvaya.parts: सर्व (all) + यज्ञ (sacrifice)

verses.explanation: Why the incomplete address matters: the offering arrives, but the offerer's *aim* terminates at the intermediary — and one travels to one's aim (8.6's law). Cyavanti, they fall back: not punished, simply returned from a finite destination. The loss is not of the gift but of the giver's own trajectory.
verses.connection: Completes 9.23: received by him, yes — but the worshiper journeys only as far as they knowingly sent themselves.
verses.reflection: Aim the offering correctly once today: to the Enjoyer of all sacrifice, by name.
verses.background: Krishna audits religion itself: the Veda-knowers who drink soma reach heaven and, merit spent, return — coming and going, ruled by desire. But for those who think of Me with no other thought, I carry what they lack and preserve what they have; worshipers reach what they worship — My devotees come to Me.
verses.hook: Why do worshippers of other gods fall back into rebirth?

views.text: As the Self of the deities he presides over every sacrifice (citing 8.4); not knowing him and not offering him the fruit, they go by the southern path and return when the merit runs out.
'Lord' means he alone grants every reward; the same rite yields a small, falling reward or the Supreme Person himself, depending only on the intention behind it.
Those who see the Lord as the inner controller in every deity they worship do not return; only those who miss this fall back.
The celestial gods can grant material favours but cannot free anyone from birth and death, since they are not free themselves; only devotion offered to God Himself leads to His abode.

bhūtāni yānti bhūtejyā yānti madyājino'pi mām
verses.essence: Votaries of the gods go to the gods; votaries of the ancestors go to the ancestors; worshipers of spirits go to the spirits; and those who sacrifice to me come to me.
verses.translation: The worshippers of the gods go to them; to the manes go the ancestor-worshippers; to the deities who preside over the elements go their worshippers; but My devotees come to Me.

anvaya.parts: मद् (me) + याजिन् (sacrificer): those who sacrifice to me

verses.explanation: The law of 9.24 written as a fare table, four lines, no exceptions: destination equals devotion. Each row is honored — the gods' votaries truly reach the gods — and each fare costs the same coin: a life's orientation. The last line's quiet asymmetry is the chapter's whole argument: for identical fare, one route ends where there is no further terminus.
verses.connection: The summary timetable of 9.20–24: every aim arrives — so aim at the unsurpassable.
verses.reflection: Notice the law of destinations: you arrive at what you worship. Check your itinerary tonight.
verses.background: Krishna audits religion itself: the Veda-knowers who drink soma reach heaven and, merit spent, return — coming and going, ruled by desire. But for those who think of Me with no other thought, I carry what they lack and preserve what they have; worshipers reach what they worship — My devotees come to Me.
verses.hook: Where do people go after death, depending on what they worship?

views.text: The effort is the same either way; only through ignorance do people fail to worship the Lord exclusively and so gain lesser results. The 'beings' are Vināyaka, the Mothers and the like.
Vrata means intention. The same rites, done with the resolve to worship Vasudeva, whose body the gods, ancestors and spirits are, reach him; those who stop at the gods perish with them.
The gods are finite, so their votaries return; the Lord's worshippers reach Nārāyaṇa, imperishable supreme bliss.
Worshippers rise only as high as what they worship, like water in a pipe: heaven, the ancestors or spirits, so to reach the highest one must worship the Supreme.

verses.devanagari:

tadahaṃ bhaktyupahṛtamaśnāmi prayatātmanaḥ
verses.essence: A leaf, a flower, a fruit, water — whoever offers these to me with devotion, that offering of love from a pure heart, I accept.
verses.translation: Whoever offers Me with devotion a leaf, a flower, a fruit or a little water that, so offered devotedly by the pure-minded, I accept.

adjective, neuter, accusative singular (describing the offering)
anvaya.parts: भक्ति (devotion) + उपहृत (brought near, offered): brought with devotion

anvaya.parts: प्रयत (restrained, purified) + आत्मन् (self, mind): one whose mind is pure

verses.explanation: From cosmic fare-tables to a leaf in an open palm. The price of reaching the unsurpassable is set at whatever the poorest hand can hold — provided it carries bhakti. Aśnāmi: he does not merely accept but *partakes*, eats, as a parent eats a child's offered crumb; temple practice takes the word literally. The operative clause is bhaktyā prayatātmanaḥ — offered with love, by a purified heart. The economy of 9.22 in miniature: love is the only currency, and the smallest denomination clears. Grace runs on sincerity, not substance.
verses.connection: The most quoted verse of practical devotion: the door of 9.25's highest destination, shown to be unlocked.
verses.reflection: Offer the smallest thing today — a leaf, a sip of water, a minute — with actual love. It is enough.
verses.background: The chapter ends in the widest opening of the poem: a leaf, a flower, fruit, water offered with love is accepted; make every act an offering; I am equal to all, yet My lovers are in Me; even the worst, rightly resolved, swiftly turns righteous; no one devoted to Me is ever lost — whatever their birth. Then the fourfold instruction: mind on Me, devoted, sacrificing, bowing.
verses.hook: What kind of offering does God actually accept?

refs.note: The same verse appears where Krishna, eating Sudama's dry rice, says He gladly eats a leaf, flower, fruit or water offered with love.
For even a tulsī leaf and a palmful of water offered with love, God gives Himself to the devotee.

views.text: The Lord accepts whatever leaf, flower, fruit or water is presented with devotion, specifically by the pure-hearted man (prayatātman).
True devotion is love so great the devotee cannot live without offering; the all-fulfilled Lord accepts such a leaf as if receiving something far beyond his hopes.
Unlike lesser gods, the supreme Lord is not pleased by costly sacrifices but by devotion alone; he eats even a leaf out of grace toward the devotee.
Leaf and flower are only symbols, as with Sudāmā's parched rice and Śabarī's berries; build the golden temple in your heart. Aśnāmi literally means 'eat', and by implication 'accept'.
God cares nothing for the value of an offering, only for the love in it; even a leaf or water given with a pure heart pleases Him, as His meal at Vidurani's hut showed.

verses.explanation: The leaf-and-water principle expanded to the whole of life: not new acts added, but every existing act re-addressed — mad-arpaṇam, made over to me. Doing, eating, offering, giving, austerity: the day's full inventory, ordinary and sacred alike, becomes liturgy without changing a single item on it. Where 9.26 blessed the smallest gift, this verse takes in the whole calendar. It is the karma-yoga of chapter 3 restated with its recipient named again: the kitchen, the desk, the road — all altar.
verses.connection: Universalizes 9.26: from one devotional offering to existence itself as the offering.
verses.reflection: Convert the day wholesale: whatever you do, eat, give, undergo — append silently, 'this is offered.'
verses.background: The chapter ends in the widest opening of the poem: a leaf, a flower, fruit, water offered with love is accepted; make every act an offering; I am equal to all, yet My lovers are in Me; even the worst, rightly resolved, swiftly turns righteous; no one devoted to Me is ever lost — whatever their birth. Then the fourfold instruction: mind on Me, devoted, sacrificing, bowing.
verses.hook: How can ordinary daily actions become an offering?

refs.note: Whatever one does with body, speech, mind and senses should be offered to Narayan, the same instruction this verse gives.
Devotion means offering every activity to God and feeling deep longing whenever one forgets Him.

views.text: 'Whatever you do' covers even spontaneous acts like walking, not only rites enjoined by scripture; gifts and austerities follow, and all of it is to be dedicated.
Offer not just the acts but yourself as doer and enjoyer, and the deities you worship, since all belong to and depend on the Lord as his śeṣa, existing for him.
The simplest method of yoga: consecrate every act and greed slowly dissolves into giving, like a river losing its name in the sea. Take it up from today.
Devotion is not limited to the temple; every action, meal and duty should be offered to God while doing it, not by a closing mantra, which turns ordinary life into service.

verses.explanation: The mechanism stated: what is given away can no longer bind the giver. Actions offered in 9.27 stop depositing their fruits — fair or foul — in the doer's account; the ledger simply closes. Sannyāsa-yoga: renunciation not as leaving acts but as leaving ownership of them, the chapter's working synthesis of all earlier paths.
verses.connection: The fruit of 9.27's re-addressing: karma's bookkeeping ends, and the freed account-holder comes home.
verses.reflection: Walk free of one result today, good or bad, by having offered the act before doing it.

Then the fourfold instruction: mind on Me, devoted, sacrificing, bowing.
verses.hook: How can you be freed from the results of good and bad actions?

views.text: Sannyāsa is the dedication of actions to the Lord, and it is yoga because it still involves action; freed from karma's bonds while living, one reaches him when the body falls.
Seeing oneself as the Lord's śeṣa and every act as his worship frees one from the countless ancient karmas that block the way to him.
The renunciation-yoga is to regard every act as absorbed in the Lord, or born of him.
Every action carries some harm, and even good karma binds the soul to heaven; dedicating all actions to God's pleasure removes selfishness and frees one from both kinds of results.

verses.devanagari:
समोऽहं सर्वभूतेषु न मे द्वेष्योऽस्ति न प्रियः ।
ये भजन्ति तु मां भक्त्या मयि ते तेषु चाप्यहम्॥
verses.transliteration:
samo'haṃ sarvabhūteṣu na me dveṣyo'sti na priyaḥ
ye bhajanti tu māṃ bhaktyā mayi te teṣu cāpyaham
verses.essence: I am the same toward all beings; none is hateful to me, none dear. But those who worship me with devotion — they are in me, and I too am in them.
verses.translation: The same am I to all beings; to Me there is none hateful or dear; but those who worship Me with devotion are in Me and I am also in them.

anvaya.parts: सर्व (all) + भूत (being)

anvaya.form: pronoun, genitive singular (to me, for me)
gerundive, masculine, nominative singular (to be hated)
relative pronoun, masculine, nominative plural (those who)

verses.explanation: Two truths that look like rivals, held in one breath: perfect impartiality — none hated, none favored — and yet a real, mutual indwelling with those who love him: they are in me, and I in them. The commentators resolve it with fire: it warms whoever draws near and refuses no one, yet only those who come close feel it. His sameness never wavers; the devotee steps into the always-shining. Grace is not favoritism; it is exposure. Divine impartiality is the constancy; intimacy is what reciprocity does with it.
verses.connection: Reconciles the chapter's universal God with its intimate one — equality below, communion above.
verses.reflection: Trust the impartial sun today: equally on all, and intimate with whoever steps outside.
verses.background: The chapter ends in the widest opening of the poem: a leaf, a flower, fruit, water offered with love is accepted; make every act an offering; I am equal to all, yet My lovers are in Me; even the worst, rightly resolved, swiftly turns righteous; no one devoted to Me is ever lost — whatever their birth. Then the fourfold instruction: mind on Me, devoted, sacrificing, bowing.
verses.hook: Does God favour some beings over others?

views.text: The Lord is like fire, which removes cold only from those who come near. Devotees are in him by their own nature, not because he loves them more, so there is no hatred toward others.
No one seeking refuge is rejected or preferred for birth, form or learning; taking refuge is the only test. He abides in such devotees as though they were his superiors.
Like sunlight that fills everything but reflects only in a clean mirror, the Lord shows himself in minds that devotion has cleansed; he has no more attachment than the sun has for the mirror.
God is equal to all and gives grace by one law, according to how people surrender; like rain that becomes grain or thorn by where it falls, the difference lies in the receiving heart.

verses.devanagari:
अपि चेत्सुदुराचारो भजते मामनन्यभाक् ।
साधुरेव स मन्तव्यः सम्यग्व्यवसितो हि सः॥

api cetsudurācāro bhajate māmananyabhāk
sādhureva sa mantavyaḥ samyagvyavasito hi saḥ
verses.essence: Even if one of very evil conduct worships me with undivided devotion, that one must be reckoned righteous — for the resolve is rightly set.
verses.translation: Even if the most sinful worships Me, with devotion to none else, he too should indeed by regarded as righteous for he has rightly resolved.

verses.explanation: The most generous sentence in the scripture's most generous chapter: take the worst résumé — su-durācāraḥ — and one undivided turning outweighs it, mantavyaḥ, *must* be so reckoned, an instruction to the judging world as much as a comfort to the sinner. The logic: conduct is the past; vyavasāya, the set of the will, is the trajectory — and persons are their trajectories.
verses.connection: The chapter's amnesty: 9.26's open door, confirmed open even to the disgraced.
verses.reflection: Refuse to finalize anyone today — including yourself. One true resolve re-titles a whole past.
verses.background: The chapter ends in the widest opening of the poem: a leaf, a flower, fruit, water offered with love is accepted; make every act an offering; I am equal to all, yet My lovers are in Me; even the worst, rightly resolved, swiftly turns righteous; no one devoted to Me is ever lost — whatever their birth. Then the fourfold instruction: mind on Me, devoted, sacrificing, bowing.
verses.hook: Can someone with a very bad past still be considered good?

refs.note: The world knows that Valmiki became a saint by chanting God's name even in reverse order.

views.text: Even a man of very condemnable conduct who worships the Lord with a mind given to no one else must be deemed good, since he has resolved rightly and has virtuous intentions.
Such a person ranks with the jñānins already praised and must be honoured; set against so rare a resolve, his breaches of rule are a negligible fault.
His right resolve is the decision 'I will be fulfilled by worshipping the Supreme Lord alone', seeing even other gods as Vāsudeva and turning to no other.
The holy resolve itself turns the life around: Ratnākara became Vālmīki. Remembrance of God destroys sins that particular penances cannot.
Devotion can reform even the worst sinner, as Ajamil and Valmiki show; one who resolves on exclusive devotion should be seen as righteous because of that pure intention.

verses.devanagari:
क्षिप्रं भवति धर्मात्मा शश्वच्छान्तिं निगच्छति ।
कौन्तेय प्रतिजानीहि न मे भक्तः प्रणश्यति॥
verses.transliteration:
kṣipraṃ bhavati dharmātmā śaśvacchāntiṃ nigacchati
kaunteya pratijānīhi na me bhaktaḥ praṇaśyati
verses.essence: Swiftly such a one becomes a soul of dharma and attains lasting peace. Kaunteya, declare it: my devotee never perishes.
verses.translation: Soon he becomes righteous and attains to eternal peace; O Arjuna, proclaim thou for certain that My devotee never perishes.

anvaya.parts: धर्म (righteousness) + आत्मन् (self, mind): one whose mind is set in dharma

verses.explanation: The promise of 9.30 secured, with a startling delegation: pratijānīhi — *you* proclaim it, Arjuna. Śrīdhara pictures the scene: go into the hall of quarrelling disputants, raise your arm, and declare it without fear, to the sound of drums. The pledge is placed in the devotee's own mouth. Na me bhaktaḥ praṇaśyati: four words generations have gripped in the dark.
verses.connection: Seals 9.30's amnesty into oath — and makes Arjuna its guarantor.
verses.reflection: Say the guarantee to someone who needs it, or to yourself: My devotee is never lost.
verses.background: The chapter ends in the widest opening of the poem: a leaf, a flower, fruit, water offered with love is accepted; make every act an offering; I am equal to all, yet My lovers are in Me; even the worst, rightly resolved, swiftly turns righteous; no one devoted to Me is ever lost — whatever their birth. Then the fourfold instruction: mind on Me, devoted, sacrificing, bowing.
verses.hook: What becomes of a devotee who changes course toward God?

views.text: The strength of the inner resolve makes him drop his outward wrongdoing; Arjuna is told to proclaim boldly that one who has given his inner being to the Lord is never ruined.
Rajas and tamas are uprooted, and 'dharma' here is the bhakti named at 9.3; despite past misconduct he reaches a state of no return and soon perfect devotion.
Arjuna, worried that hair-splitting debaters will not accept this, is urged to enter their assembly with drums, raise his arm and make the pledge fearlessly.
Virtues cannot be acquired without purifying the mind through devotion; Krishna has Arjun declare that His devotee never perishes because the Lord may break His own word but never His devotee's.

verses.devanagari:
मां हि पार्थ व्यपाश्रित्य येऽपि स्युः पापयोनयः ।
स्त्रियो वैश्यास्तथा शूद्रास्तेऽपि यान्ति परां गतिम्॥
verses.transliteration:
māṃ hi pārtha vyapāśritya ye'pi syuḥ pāpayonayaḥ
striyo vaiśyāstathā śūdrāste'pi yānti parāṃ gatim
verses.essence: For those who take refuge in me, Partha — whatever their birth, women, merchants, even laborers — they too reach the supreme goal.
verses.translation: For, taking refuge in Me, they also who, O Arjuna, may be of a sinful birth women, Vaisyas as well as Sudras attain the Supreme Goal.
