verses.explanation: Read against its era, this verse is a door blown open: every group its society's ritual system kept from the highest pursuits — listed here in the period's own blunt categories — is declared eligible, te 'pi yānti parāṁ gatim, for the very summit. The path of refuge asks no pedigree, gender, or caste; it asks only the turning, mām vyapāśritya, taking refuge in me. Devotional movements across the centuries have leaned on this verse, and saints of every excluded origin are its living commentary.
verses.connection: Extends 9.30–31's amnesty across the social order: the royal road is public, in the fullest sense.
verses.reflection: Wherever you started from, the summit is open — let no biography disqualify you from refuge today.
verses.background: The chapter ends in the widest opening of the poem: a leaf, a flower, fruit, water offered with love is accepted; make every act an offering; I am equal to all, yet My lovers are in Me; even the worst, rightly resolved, swiftly turns righteous; no one devoted to Me is ever lost — whatever their birth. Then the fourfold instruction: mind on Me, devoted, sacrificing, bowing.
verses.hook: Does birth, gender or social class bar anyone from the highest goal?

refs.note: Yoga practice must be done in a pure place and posture, an example of the strict rules other paths impose.
Devotion has no rules of place or time, supporting the verse's claim that it is open to everyone.

views.text: Even those born of sin, whom the Lord names as women, Vaiśyas and Śūdras, reach the highest Goal by accepting him as their refuge.
Those 'of sinful birth' are animals, birds and the like; 'women' stands for the ignorant. Commentators who restrict the verse are rebuked for limiting the Lord's grace, which is for all.
If devotion frees even those barred from Vedic study, it is no wonder it purifies one who has merely strayed in conduct.
Birth is immaterial and devotion everything: Gajendra the elephant, Prahlāda the demon, Raidās the cobbler and Śabarī all reached the Lord.
Other paths set strict conditions of qualification, ritual or place, but devotion is open to anyone, anywhere, whatever their birth or gender; God looks only at the love in the heart.

verses.devanagari:
किं पुनर्ब्राह्मणाः पुण्या भक्ता राजर्षयस्तथा ।
अनित्यमसुखं लोकमिमं प्राप्य भजस्व माम्॥
verses.transliteration:

anityamasukhaṃ lokamimaṃ prāpya bhajasva mām

verses.translation: How much more (easily) then the hold Brahmins and devoted royal saints (attain the goal); having come to this impermanent and unhappy world, do thou worship Me.

adjective, masculine, nominative plural (describing royal sages)

anvaya.form: imperative, 2nd person singular, middle voice (a command)

verses.explanation: The a-fortiori turn: if the door stands open to the excluded, those born holding every advantage have least excuse to linger outside it. Then the chapter's bluntest line about the venue: anityam asukham — impermanent and, on net, not happy. Not despair; a clear-eyed travel advisory, with the one worthwhile activity here named in two words: bhajasva mām.
verses.connection: Turns 9.32's universal access into universal urgency: whoever you are, the world won't hold — worship.
verses.reflection: You hold an unfleeting chance in a fleeting world — spend one deliberate hour of it on the highest.
verses.background: The chapter ends in the widest opening of the poem: a leaf, a flower, fruit, water offered with love is accepted; make every act an offering; I am equal to all, yet My lovers are in Me; even the worst, rightly resolved, swiftly turns righteous; no one devoted to Me is ever lost — whatever their birth. Then the fourfold instruction: mind on Me, devoted, sacrificing, bowing.
verses.hook: If even the lowly reach God, what should the well-placed do?

views.text: Having come into this ephemeral, miserable human world, a human life that is a means to Liberation, Arjuna should worship the Lord; holy Brāhmaṇas and devout royal sages succeed all the more surely.
Each adjective gives a reason: the world is impermanent, so do not delay; it is joyless, so give up striving for pleasure here, and worship.
A human birth is hard to get and even the gods envy it; to spend it without aiming at Self-realisation is to live in vain.

If even sinners are assured success through devotion, the virtuous and well-born have every reason for confidence; recognising the world as temporary and full of misery, they should not waste their advantages.

verses.devanagari:
मन्मना भव मद्भक्तो मद्याजी मां नमस्कुरु ।
मामेवैष्यसि युक्त्वैवमात्मानं मत्परायणः॥
verses.transliteration:
manmanā bhava madbhakto madyājī māṃ namaskuru
māmevaiṣyasi yuktvaivamātmānaṃ matparāyaṇaḥ
verses.essence: Fix your mind on me, be my devotee, sacrifice to me, bow to me. Thus harnessing yourself, with me as the supreme goal, you will come to me.
verses.translation: Fix thy mind on Me; by devoted to Me; sacrifice unto Me; bow down to Me; having thus united thy whole self to Me, taking Me as the supreme goal, thou shalt come unto Me.

मद् (me) + भक्त (devotee)

verses.explanation: The royal secret reduced to four imperatives small enough to carry into battle: mind here, heart here, acts here, body bowed here — man-manā, mad-bhakta, mad-yājī, namaskuru. Thought, love, work, humility: the four limbs of a life, all given one direction. So central is the formula that the Gita repeats its first line word for word at its own climax (18.65), as if to say: if everything else is forgotten, keep this. Mat-parāyaṇaḥ: with me as the way and the destination both.
verses.connection: The chapter's seal — and the seed of the scripture's final instruction nine chapters later.
verses.reflection: Do the fourfold once before sleep: mind on Him, heart to Him, an offering, a bow.
verses.background: The chapter ends in the widest opening of the poem: a leaf, a flower, fruit, water offered with love is accepted; make every act an offering; I am equal to all, yet My lovers are in Me; even the worst, rightly resolved, swiftly turns righteous; no one devoted to Me is ever lost — whatever their birth. Then the fourfold instruction: mind on Me, devoted, sacrificing, bowing.
verses.hook: What final instruction does Krishna give to reach Him?

views.text: Ātmānam is to be joined with mām: 'you will reach me, who am thus the Self' of all beings and also their supreme goal.
Fixing the mind means an unbroken flow like a stream of oil on the Lord in his full form and qualities; worship is the service of one who knows himself wholly the Lord's śeṣa.
Fix head, heart and hands on the Lord and surrender the whole being without reserve; then the whole life is transformed.
Closing the chapter, Krishna asks Arjun to become His devotee: fix the mind on Him, worship Him and bow down in humility, which removes pride; such communion surely leads to God-realization.
